questions.prompt: Directions: Suppose your class plans to invite some former graduates to share their job experiences with the students. As the organizer of the activity, you are now to write an invitation letter to the invited speakers on behalf of your class. You will have 30 minutes to write the letter.You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.correctAnswer:
Dear Ms. Chen,

On behalf of our class, I would like to invite you to share your job experiences with current students at our university. As a former graduate, you could offer valuable insight into the transition from campus study to professional work.

We plan to hold the event next Friday afternoon in the student activity room. A short talk of about twenty minutes could introduce your career path, followed by a discussion in which students ask questions. We would especially appreciate your advice on preparing applications, developing useful skills and dealing with difficulties in the first year of work.

If the proposed time is inconvenient, we would be happy to make another arrangement. Please let us know whether you can attend and whether any equipment is required. Thank you for considering our invitation. We look forward to learning from your experience and welcoming you back to campus.

Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

questions.hint: 代表班级邀请毕业生，写分享主题、时间地点、流程和确认方式。
questions.explanation:
以下为按题意独立写成的参考范文，作文没有唯一答案。邀请对象是毕业生而不是招聘单位；可调整时间和询问设备使书信礼貌完整。示范时间地点可更换。

信以班级名义邀请毕业生分享工作经验，开头说明活动目的，主体给主题、示范时间地点及分享内容，末尾询问安排并期待回复。on behalf of是代表，share experiences with是与某人分享经历，confirm availability是确认能否到场。邀请函需礼貌且让嘉宾知道自己要做什么；不要误写成学生求职信。时间地点由范文设定，可替换；真实题面多余空格不改变邀请毕业生这一任务。

练习方法：先用提示列三段提纲，在30分钟内独立写作，再按下方标准逐项打分；把失分最多的一段重写。参考范文约152词（缩写、连字符词按一词，含标题或书信称呼落款），满足120–180词要求；评分用于练习自检，不代表官方阅卷分数。
rubric: 练习自评总分15分：题目覆盖0–6＋结构0–4＋语言0–5，先独立写完再对照；观点不同于范文也可得满分，只要有合理支持。
题目覆盖0–6分：该题检查——代表班级邀请毕业生，写分享主题、时间地点、流程和确认方式。。6分=任务完整且有具体理由/活动/例证；4–5分=切题但细节偏薄；2–3分=遗漏主要任务；0–1分=基本离题。
结构0–4分：4分=开头明确任务、主体按逻辑展开、结尾回扣，段间自然；3分=顺序清楚但局部衔接生硬；1–2分=跳跃或机械罗列；0分=内容难以组织理解。
语言0–5分：5分=语法和用词基本准确、句型有变化；3–4分=少量错误但不影响理解；1–2分=反复出现时态、主谓一致或搭配错误并影响阅读；0分=多数句子不能理解。
格式与修订：按原题保持120–180词；新闻/书信/提案用对应体裁，明确要求的首句逐字保留。若超限、少写任务或缺必要格式，先修改再评分，不把字数达标当作内容满分。

It is likely that the "first to arrive and last to leave" mentality is no longer relevant, but should be replaced by a regard for the quality of an employee's contribution to the organization. This means that work should be measured in terms of the quality of the work, not just the quality of the process. As remote work is largely unobservable to supervisors, employers need to think about how they can objectively measure the quality of work in a way that is consistent for employees of similar rank.

Focusing on output alone can have unintended consequences. Employers should think instead about the values and soft skills they want to emphasize in a remote work environment. Qualities like flexibility and the ability to work under minimal supervision might become critical.

This allows managers to both keep an eye on struggling employees and provide ongoing feedback on how employees are adapting to their new work environment.

Compensation also needs to be revisited. The purpose of performance evaluation is ultimately to determine how to reward employees for their work. This means that pay structures need to adapt to the reality of working from home. However, organizations also need to be honest with employees about the financial impact of COVID-19.

For organizations that have struggled to keep the lights on due to the pandemic, this might mean thinking of non-financial ways to reward employees, like unpaid time off or flexible work schedules. Focusing on output alone can have unintended consequences. Employers should think instead about the values and soft skills they want to emphasize in a remote work environment. Qualities like flexibility and the ability to work under minimal supervision might become critical.

Much has been written about the importance of timely feedback. In the context of a global pandemic(大流行病), firms may want to provide additional support to employees by providing more frequent communication. This allows managers to both keep an eye on struggling employees and provide ongoing feedback on how employees are adapting to their new work environment.

Compensation also needs to be revisited. The purpose of performance evaluation is ultimately to determine how to reward employees for their work. This means that pay structures need to adapt to the reality of working from home. However, organizations also need to be honest with employees about the financial impact of COVID-19.

For organizations that have struggled to keep the lights on due to the pandemic, this might mean thinking of non-financial ways to reward employees, like unpaid time off or flexible work schedules. Employers can also consider how to bundle different types of compensation to help employees cope with their unique situations.
